newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan profits jump in fourth quarter.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan profits jump in fourth quarter.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. Monday reported sharply higher fourth-quarter profits as revenues soared across the range of its investment banking businesses.
Earnings rose 14 percent to $419 million, or 2.04 a share, from $366 million, or $1.80 a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues grew to $1.805 billion from $1.518 billion.

"Our business grew substantially in 1996 and produced strong results across the range of our advisory, capital raising, asset management, risk management and trading activities," said Douglas Warner III, chairman of the company.

Trading revenues rose 39 percent to $512 million from $369 million in the 1995 fourth quarter. Investment banking revenues rose 75 percent to $277 million from $158 million as the Wall Street firm took on higher levels of advisory, syndication and underwriting activities.
Securities Data Corp. ranked J.P. Morgan the sixth-largest underwriter of U.S. debt and stock issues and fifth-largest adviser in completed mergers and acquisitions worldwide in 1996.
Investment management fees rose 17 percent to $182 million from $156 million mainly as a result of net new business.
Net interest revenue was barely changed at $484 million.
Operating expenses rose 21 percent to $1.197 billion from $990 million as compensation grew in line with improved earnings and costs rose with increased activity in client businesses.
J.P. Morgan's stock rose $2.375 to $102.125 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
